explanation: India is generally described as a high-context, relationship-oriented culture where communication relies heavily on tone and nonverbal cues, and more reserved eye contact toward elders or superiors can be a sign of deference in some settings. Norms vary widely by region, generation, and whether you're in a traditional or Westernized urban professional environment, so there isn't one fixed rule, and direct eye contact between peers is generally normal and unremarkable.
local_tip: Keep eye contact natural and moderate; don't force intense or prolonged eye contact with someone senior to you, and take cues from how your counterpart engages.

also_check.note: Prolonged direct eye contact can feel intimidating; brief, softer eye contact is preferred, especially toward superiors.
Direct eye contact is generally expected as a sign of honesty and confidence, including in business.
Eye contact norms differ by gender; prolonged eye contact between unrelated men and women is often avoided.
